--- title: "Monitoring Right-Wing Extremism (RWE)" subtitle: "Discourse, Protest, Violence" author: "[Dr. Michael C. Zeller](https://michaelzeller.de)" format: revealjs: # footer: "" slide-number: c/t toc: FALSE toc-depth: 1 toc-title: Agenda for the day menu: TRUE theme: dracula # blood background-transition: fade incremental: false embed-resources: true # datadownload: # excel1: "demos_2005-2024sep_geo.xlsx" # excel2: "poldem-protest_30.csv" # runtime: shiny bibliography: ../../../../../../../library.bib --- ## ::: {style="text-align: center; color:white; font-size:45px; margin-top: 100px;"} *__discourses__* frame issues, providing basis for connection and mobilisation of collective action ::: ::: {.fragment style="text-align: center; color:white; font-size:45px;"} *__protest__* is a prominent method of attempting to set political agendas and advance (movement) goals ::: ::: {.fragment style="text-align: center; color:white; font-size:45px;"} *__violence__* is a common outgrowth of extremist discourse and collective action---presenting a challenge to societies and a public policy concern for state actors ::: ## Complications of monitoring RWE - fuzzy boundaries of 'extremism' - different degrees of activity in different contexts---but also different national reporting and monitoring standards + e.g., [RTV](https://www.sv.uio.no/c-rex/english/resources/rtv-dataset/) difficulty tracking violence beyond Western Europe; [OSCE hate crime](https://hatecrime.osce.org/) monitoring - sensitivities about historical memory issues, involvement/complicity of political parties, timing of monitoring and public communication thereof ## Purpose of the presentation {visibility="hidden"} - introduce some recent/current and/or larger projects monitoring RWE discourse, protest, and violence + link these three phenomena, drawing on scholarly literature - put some data at your fingertips - discuss some recurring issues in policy and policymaking of RWE monitoring (and interventions) ## outline {visibility="hidden"} OUTLINE (15-20 minutes): - Discourses [@ahmed2021UnitingFarRight; @bailard2024KeepYourHeads; @Giugni2005; @JohnsonETAL2019; @kasimov2023DecentralizedHateSustained; @vicenova2020RoleDigitalMedia; @volker2024DiscourseNetworksFar] + common topics: climate politics, COVID-19, EU, gender, migration, (Islamist) terrorism, Ukraine * conspiracy beliefs: Great Replacement + Transnational connections (Heft et al.) + Facebook discourse data? + RWE demos in Germany data - quick text analysis of Mottos * term frequency bars * td-idf network (nodes coloured by organiser: NPD/Heimat, Rechte, III. Weg, ProChemnitz; other as grey) - Demonstrations [@castelligattinara2024WhenFarRight; @rocchetti2025DynamicsProtestsCounterprotests; @Virchow2007a; @vullers2022DoesCountermobilizationContain; @Weisskircher2019] + PolDem/ACLED overview? * issue_xeno (Yes=1) * actor_party_right (Yes=1) [compare with actor_party_left] + FRGB on UK, FARPO on Italy * year-month bar plot * ggiraph by region/Kreis * mapview + RWE demos in Germany data * year-month bar plot * ggiraph by region/Kreis * mapview - Violence [@bjorgo2020WhyNordicResistance; @dasilva2022StreetSoldiersPolitical; @dejuan2025RightWingTerrorMedia; @JostETAL2025; @koopmans1996ExplainingRiseRacist; @krause2023DoesRightWingViolence; @Meadowcroft2017; @Ravndal2018; @whittington2024FarRightExtremismElections] + OSCE hate crime data * notes about difficulties of comparing 'hate crimes' across country contexts + RTV - lethal violence - Summarising/Diagnosing the problem(s) # RWE Discourse {background-color="#BD93F9"} ::: {style="margin-top: -40px;"} - large overlap between different '**far-right**' discources [@ahmed2021UnitingFarRight] + broadly, RW 'extremism' *rejects democratic principles* ::: {.fragment .fade-up style="margin-top: -45px;"} - (online) discourses motivate (offline) activity and violence [@bailard2024KeepYourHeads; @Giugni2005; @JohnsonETAL2019; @kasimov2023DecentralizedHateSustained] ::: {style="margin-top: -50px;"} > intensifying expressions of grievances online predict participation in offline violence [@bailard2024KeepYourHeads] ::: ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-up style="margin-top: -35px;"} - discursive activity can also contribute to normalising radical/extreme actors in politics and public life [@volker2024DiscourseNetworksFar] ::: ::: ## Common topics across contexts - constantly shifting, but in recent years frequently: ::: {.fragment .fade-up style="margin-top: -45px;"} [climate]{style="color:#1B9E77;"}, [COVID-19]{style="color:#D95F02;"}, [EU]{style="color:#7570B3;"}, [gender]{style="color:#E7298A;"}, [migration]{style="color:#66A61E;"}, [terrorism]{style="color:#E6AB02;"}, [Ukraine]{style="color:#A6761D;"} ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-up style="margin-top: -20px;"} ![Proportion of Facebook posts about these topics by RWE groups from these countries (2021-2024)](rwe_topics.png){width=650} ::: ## Gender in focus [@tronina2026TransnationalizationAntiGenderPolitics] - common *discourses* can drive activism in different contexts - transnational set of SMOs campaigning against 'gender', for example: + framing it in opposition to 'family' + likening **gender** and **LGBT** to 'profanity' and 'propaganda' - investigating this activity through Twitter/X accounts of SMOs in [Croatia (9)]{style="color:forestgreen;"}, [Germany (26)]{style="color:darkorange;"}, [France (41)]{style="color:goldenrod;"}, [Italy (43)]{style="color:violet;"}, and [Poland (29)]{style="color:cadetblue;"} ## Gender in focus [@tronina2026TransnationalizationAntiGenderPolitics] Most Transnationally Connective Hashtags Per Year ![](tronina/tronina1.png) ## Gender in focus [@tronina2026TransnationalizationAntiGenderPolitics] Most Transnationally Connective Hashtags Per Year *[Dissemination]{style="color:cadetblue;"}* - getting the word out ![](tronina/tronina2.png) ## Gender in focus [@tronina2026TransnationalizationAntiGenderPolitics] Most Transnationally Connective Hashtags Per Year *[Dissemination]{style="color:cadetblue;"}* - getting the word out ![](tronina/tronina3.png) ## Gender in focus [@tronina2026TransnationalizationAntiGenderPolitics] Most Transnationally Connective Hashtags Per Year *[Mobilisation]{style="color:cadetblue;"}* ![](tronina/tronina4.png) ## Gender in focus [@tronina2026TransnationalizationAntiGenderPolitics] Most Transnationally Connective Hashtags Per Year *[Extension]{style="color:cadetblue;"}* - connecting to other issues ![](tronina/tronina5.png) ## RWE news ecology [@heftTransnationalInformationEcology2021] - 'alternative news' sites/channels spread RWE *discourses* - @heftTransnationalInformationEcology2021 look at hyperlinks shared by right-wing online news sites (in Austria, Germany, United States, United Kingdom, Denmark, Sweden) in 2018 ## RWE news ecology [@heftTransnationalInformationEcology2021] - 'alternative news' sites/channels spread RWE *discourses* :::: {.columns} :::{.column width="50%"} ![](heftETAL2021.png) ::: ::: {.column width="50%" .center} - degree of transnational linkages differ by context - DE: some orgs. focus mostly domestically; others mostly internationally - SE, US: most orgs., mostly **domestically** - UK, AT, DK: most orgs., mostly **internationally** ::: :::: ## RWE protest mottos (DE) {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ::: *discourses* connect to *offline activity*: slogans of German RWE protests, some (randomly selected) examples: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.fragment style="margin-top: -10px;"} **[„Familien schützen! Homo-Propaganda stoppen!“]{style="color:#E64B35;"}** *"Protect families! Stop gay propaganda!"* ::: ::: {.fragment style="margin-top: -10px;"} **[Thüringer Heldengedenken]{style="color:#E64B35;"}** *Thuringian heroic commemoration* ::: ::: {.fragment style="margin-top: -10px;"} **[„Genug ist genug! Stoppt die Überfremdung der Heimat“ (Berlin)]{style="color:#E64B35;"}** *"Enough is enough! Stop the foreign infiltration of the homeland" (Berlin)* ::: ::: {.fragment style="margin-top: -10px;"} **[Für Meinungsfreiheit – gegen staatliche Zensur]{style="color:#E64B35;"}** *For freedom of expression – against state censorship* ::: ::: {.fragment style="margin-top: -10px;"} **[Nationale Souveränität erhalten – Deutschland raus aus der EU]{style="color:#E64B35;"}** *Maintain national sovereignty – Germany out of the EU* ::: ::: {.fragment style="margin-top: -10px;"} **[„Mein Körper gehört mir, schützt endlich unsere Kinder und Alten“]{style="color:#E64B35;"}** *“My body belongs to me, finally protects our children and the elderly”* ::: ## RWE protest mottos (DE) ::: {style="margin-top: -25px;"} discourses connect to offline activity, here: the most frequent words in German RWE protest slogans ::: ::: {style="margin-top: -25px;"} **all terms** ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## RWE protest mottos (DE) {background-color="white"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](europaeum_pres_files/figure-revealjs/mottos_netz2-1.png){width=100%} ::: ::: ::: {.absolute top=100 left=600} - nodes: RWE demonstration categories as tracked by German governments - edges: indicate strength of similarity of terms in demo. groups' 'motto' texts ::: # RWE Protest {background-color="#BD93F9"} ::: {style="margin-top: -50px;"} - demonstrations serve many purposes for RWE: building *solidarity/collective identity* [@Virchow2007a; @Meadowcroft2017], attracting *media attention* [@castelligattinara2024WhenFarRight], recurrent dates for *networking* [@Zeller2026CUP], *agenda setting* and building momentum for far-right parties [@Weisskircher2019] ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-up style="margin-top: -50px;"} - *countermobilisation* often emerges to oppose RWE protest---with mixed results [@vullers2022DoesCountermobilizationContain; @rocchetti2025DynamicsProtestsCounterprotests; @Zeller2021_hess; @Zeller2025ejpr] ::: ::: {.fragment .fade-up style="margin-top: -50px;"} - several projects track RWE protest activity + some comparative: [Poldem](https://poldem.eui.eu/); [ACLED](https://acleddata.com/); myriad country-specific projects ::: ## RWE Protest - overview {background-color="white"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

font-size:45px;"}** **[UK]{style="color:#4682B4; font-size:45px;"}** **[Germany]{style="color:#32CD32; font-size:45px;"}** ::: ```{ojs} //| echo: false // Combine the datasets Italy = [ {Year: 2008, Num: 42}, {Year: 2009, Num: 117}, {Year: 2010, Num: 269}, {Year: 2011, Num: 233}, {Year: 2012, Num: 196}, {Year: 2013, Num: 225}, {Year: 2014, Num: 228}, {Year: 2015, Num: 190}, {Year: 2016, Num: 138}, {Year: 2017, Num: 54}, {Year: 2018, Num: 26} ] UK = [ {Year: 2009, Num: 40}, {Year: 2010, Num: 98}, {Year: 2011, Num: 148}, {Year: 2012, Num: 116}, {Year: 2013, Num: 161}, {Year: 2014, Num: 149}, {Year: 2015, Num: 123}, {Year: 2016, Num: 83}, {Year: 2017, Num: 84}, {Year: 2018, Num: 107}, {Year: 2019, Num: 107} ] Germany = [ {Year: 2005, Num: 187}, {Year: 2006, Num: 151}, {Year: 2007, Num: 129}, {Year: 2008, Num: 103}, {Year: 2009, Num: 137}, {Year: 2010, Num: 85}, {Year: 2011, Num: 142}, {Year: 2012, Num: 132}, {Year: 2013, Num: 186}, {Year: 2014, Num: 219}, {Year: 2015, Num: 491}, {Year: 2016, Num: 330}, {Year: 2017, Num: 107}, {Year: 2018, Num: 129}, {Year: 2019, Num: 174}, {Year: 2020, Num: 151}, {Year: 2021, Num: 89}, {Year: 2022, Num: 143}, {Year: 2023, Num: 196}, {Year: 2024, Num: 170} ] // Create a dropdown which dataset to display (Inputs.select) - Inputs.radio for radio buttons // FIRST VERSION: viewof dataset = Inputs.radio(["IT (farpo)", "UnitedKingdom (frgb)", "DE (bt)"], {label: "Dataset"}) viewof datasets = Inputs.checkbox( ["IT (farpo)", "UK (frgb)", "DE (bt)"], {label: "", value: ["IT (farpo)", "UK (frgb)", "DE (bt)"]} ) // Choose the corresponding dataset based on the selection // FIRST VERSION: selected_data = dataset === "IT (farpo)" ? UK : Germany // Combine the selected datasets into one array selected_data = datasets.flatMap(dataset => { if (dataset === "IT (farpo)") { return Italy.map(d => ({...d, dataset: "Italy"})); } else if (dataset === "UK (frgb)") { return UK.map(d => ({...d, dataset: "UK"})); } else if (dataset === "DE (bt)") { return Germany.map(d => ({...d, dataset: "Germany"})); } return []; }); ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false // plot as a bar plot // FIRST VERSION: Plot.plot({ // x: { // label: "", tickSize: 2, tickRotate: -45, // tickFormat: d => d.toString() // Converts the year to a string to avoid number formatting // }, // y: { // grid: true // }, // margin: 100, // marks: [ // Plot.barY(selected_data, {x: "Year", y: "Num", fill: "darkred"}) // ], // width: 1200, // height: 600, // style: { // fontSize: 30, // }, // }) // plot as a bar plot with dodged bars colored by dataset Plot.plot({ width: 1200, height: 600, marginTop: 30, marginRight: 100, marginBottom: 110, marginLeft: 100, style: { fontSize: "20px", color: "black", background: "white" }, x: { label: null, tickSize: 6, tickRotate: -45, tickFormat: d => d.toString(), tickPadding: 8, color: "black", line: true }, y: { label: "Number", grid: true, color: "black", tickSize: 6, tickPadding: 8, line: true }, color: { legend: true, domain: ["Italy", "UK", "Germany"], range: ["#FF6347", "#4682B4", "#32CD32"] }, marks: [ Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "black", strokeWidth: 1 }), Plot.barY(selected_data, { x: "Year", y: "Num", fill: "dataset" }) ] }) ``` ## RWE protest (Germany, 2005-2024) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
